Companies involved in petroleum distribution hold petroleum stockpiles among their assets, which as social attitudes increasingly favor using less carbon-intensive sources of energy, could become liabilities if their market value falls below what companies have invested to acquire and maintain them. This phenomenon is known as "asset stranding" and poses an existential threat to these companies. The significance to investors of the potential for stranding is evident, and companies ought to disclose such risks to them, <u>but it is no less important to ensure that when</u><u>      </u><u>unsustainable companies involved in petroleum distribution cease operations, those companies' employees are assisted in their transitions to other jobs.</u>
